Alyssa M.: Quick sync after the 03/18 tail-latency postmortem. We need to finalize remediation owners and decide about a short-term SLO handling strategy.
Ravi P.: I can own the KV-hotspot mitigation (runtime side). Plan: adaptive eviction + per-shard hotspots metrics. ETA 72h for a beta change.
Nora H.: I9ll take autoscaling policy + dashboard refresh. Will add a burst counter and reduce the scale-up cooldown. ETA 48h.
Alyssa M.: Do we do a public SLO change? Current p95 SLO = 200ms, infra saw 420ms during incident window. My proposal: do NOT change public SLO, set an internal "operational cushion" SLO at 280ms for ops calculations for 14 days.
Ravi P.: Agreed on internal cushion. We can flag the incident window in the public SLO dashboard so CS/customer-facing reports are accurate.
Nora H.: I9ll add a note on the public SLO dashboard: "Incident window 2026-03-18; see incident 2026-0318 for details." Also will add an internal-only tile showing buffered SLO.
Alyssa M.: Action list: Ravi -> runtime PR + perf run (3d), Nora -> autoscale + dashboard changes (2d), Alyssa -> canary plan + rollback criteria (1d). Add everything to the PM ticket and tag @oncall for the rollout window.
OncallBot: Incident 2026-03-18 | error budget impact: 4.2% | current p95: 312ms | runbook: https://go/redwood/incident/2026-0318
Ravi P.: Draft PR: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/1499 includes hotspot metric and eviction tweak. Running perf job now (logs attached).
Nora H.: Autoscale PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pull/1021 - adds burst counter + cooldown change. Updated staging dashboard at https://dash.redwood/s/ops/p95-buffered. Canary ready after runtime patch merges.
Alyssa M.: Canary checklist: 1) internal SLO doc updated, 2) canary = 5% traffic, 3) rollback if p95 > 350ms for 10m or error-rate increases by 0.5%. Any objections?
Ravi P.: No objections. Perf job shows ~20% tail improvement on synthetic load. Will finish PR tomorrow morning.
Nora H.: Scheduling 10:00 UTC canary for 5% traffic. I9ll notify SRE and CS.
Alyssa M.: OK. Post-canary we will decide whether to keep the buffer SLO or revert to original thresholds. Logging this in the postmortem ticket as follow-up tasks. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
